deviations: Decision 5 step 4 (and the Problem paragraph) claimed both intersection ellipses have semi-major r/cos(theta/2). Numeric verification (the oblique 45-degree on-both-carriers distance test) shows that claim is false for the internal-bisector ellipse: a point at (r/cos(22.5deg)) along b+ lies at distance 0.414... from each axis, not r. The correct semi-axes are: e0 in the internal bisector plane (spanned by b+ and u) has semi-major r/sin(theta/2) along b+ and semi-minor r along u; e1 in the external bisector plane (spanned by b- and u) has semi-major r/cos(theta/2) along b- and semi-minor r along u. The two semi-major axes differ for theta != pi/2 and coincide (r*sqrt(2)) only in the perpendicular Steinmetz case, exactly the case the packet's verification note said to check. Implemented with the corrected values; both t=0 witnesses satisfy the exact cylinder equations (distance r from both axes to machine precision, asserted in the tests).
disagreements: Decision 5 step 4's semi-axis formula r/cos(theta/2) is wrong for the internal-bisector ellipse (e0). The correct formula is r/sin(theta/2); r/cos(theta/2) applies only to the external-bisector ellipse (e1). The packet's own required test 2 embeds the ground truth: 'every point lies at distance r from both axes', which no construction with r/cos(theta/2) on both planes can satisfy for theta = 45deg (verified: distance 0.414 != 1). Consequence: the literal required ratio assertion 'semi-major/minor ratio is 1/cos(theta/2)' holds for e1 only; the test asserts 1/cos(theta/2) for e1 and 1/sin(theta/2) for e0, and is annotated accordingly. I implemented the corrected closed forms rather than working around the erroneous formula.
